ModifyDamageAdditive.maps_to: modify_damage_additive (strike_dummy.py:23-32), dispatched by HookSystem.modify_damage_additive (hooks.py:52-64) from DamageCmd.deal (cmds.py:56-57)
ModifyDamageAdditive.issue: Rollup of guards G1, G2 and N1 per binding rule 4. The +3 on a Strike-tagged powered attack is right and executed; the props gate has been hoisted out of the listener into the call site (G1) and the dealer/owner clause has been narrowed (G2).

guards.what: G1 (DORMANT): the `props.IsPoweredAttack()` test lives in the LISTENER in C# and in the DISPATCH SITE in the sim -- PROMPT.md bug class 27
guards.issue: MECHANISM: Hook.ModifyDamageInternal walks EVERY listener with no props gate of its own (Hook.cs:2511-2526), and each implementer decides for itself -- StrikeDummy.cs:21-23 bails on `!props.IsPoweredAttack()` (ValuePropExtensions.cs:5-12: Move and not Unpowered). The sim's HookSystem.modify_damage_additive has NO props parameter at all (hooks.py:52-58), so the test was hoisted to the caller: cmds.py:56-57 runs the additive and multiplicative chains only `if is_powered_attack(props)`. This is exactly the shape PROMPT.md bug class 27 records at Hook.ModifyBlock (paels_legion), where the hoist silently skips a listener that wanted the looser predicate. WHY IT IS DORMANT HERE, and the census is EXECUTED rather than assumed (py audit/tools/relic_probes_b15.py b15-censuses): all ELEVEN C# ModifyDamageAdditive implementers gate on IsPoweredAttack -- AccuracyPower, CalcifyPower, LeadershipPower, PhantomBladesPower, StrengthPower, TaintedPower, VigorPower, FakeStrikeDummy, MiniatureCannon, MysticLighter and StrikeDummy -- so the hoisted gate currently admits and excludes exactly the same set, and the sim's three relic-side listeners (strike_dummy.py:23, fake_strike_dummy.py:24, miniature_cannon.py:22) could not check props even if they wanted to. What makes it live: the first ModifyDamageAdditive (or ModifyDamageMultiplicative/Cap) implementer that must run on UNPOWERED damage -- at which point the fix must add the props field to the hook signature, not flip the call-site gate, because relic/brilliant_scarf G1's sibling finding needs the distinction preserved. Recorded rather than waived because 'no ported content needs the looser predicate' is today's content, not the divergence's shape (binding rule 1).

guards.what: G2 (DORMANT): C# grants the +3 when EITHER the dealer is the owner's creature OR the Strike card BELONGS to the owner; the port requires the dealer
guards.issue: MECHANISM: StrikeDummy.cs:33-36 is `if (dealer != base.Owner.Creature && cardSource.Owner != base.Owner) return 0m;` -- a conjunction of negatives, so either clause alone suffices. strike_dummy.py:30 requires `dealer is self.player` and never consults the card's owner (the sim's Card has no owner concept in this hook's signature). Two sub-cases follow. (a) A player-owned Strike-tagged card whose damage is dealt with a dealer that is not the player -- C# pays, the sim does not. (b) In multiplayer, another player's Strike dealt BY this owner's creature -- waived under the shared contract's multiplayer exclusion. REACHABILITY of (a) (DORMANT, executed census -- b15-censuses): the ported Strike-tagged cards are exactly eight (ashen_strike, perfected_strike, pommel_strike, seeker_strike, setup_strike, strike, twin_strike, ultimate_strike) and ALL EIGHT pass `dealer=ctx.player` to DamageCmd.deal -- zero exceptions -- so no ported play can reach the branch. EXECUTED demonstration of the divergence with a synthetic call (b15-misc): `DamageCmd.deal(..., 6, dealer=None, card=make_card('strike'), props=DamageProps.CARD)` deals 6 in the sim where C# deals 9. What makes it live: porting any effect that re-deals a player's Strike-tagged card's damage from another creature (a player-side summon, a 'the enemy plays your card' effect) or that passes dealer=None on a card attack.

guards.what: N1: `cardSource == null` and `!cardSource.Tags.Contains(CardTag.Strike)` (StrikeDummy.cs:25-32) vs `card is not None and 'strike' in card.tags` (strike_dummy.py:30) -- and the DOCSTRING, which describes a different rule
guards.rationale: The predicate is right: the sim models CardTag.Strike as the literal string 'strike' in a frozenset on the card, and EXECUTED (b15-censuses) exactly eight ported cards carry it. The port's own docstring (strike_dummy.py:14-15) says 'cards with "Strike" in the name', which is NOT what either side does -- the tag is data, and a Strike-named card without the tag (or a tagged card without 'strike' in its name, e.g. `setup_strike`/`ashen_strike` are fine but a future `Cleave`-style tagged card would not be) would behave differently from the comment. This is PROMPT.md bug class 24 -- a docstring that misdescribes the PORT and would point a later reader at a false gap -- so the verdict is on the CODE, which is correct, and the comment is flagged rather than filed. EXECUTED (b15-misc): a Strike gets 6 -> 9, a Bash gets 6 -> 6, and an UNPOWERED Strike gets 6 -> 6.

guards.what: N2: DynamicVar('ExtraDamage', 3m) read as BaseValue (StrikeDummy.cs:17, 37) vs EXTRA_DAMAGE = 3 (strike_dummy.py:21)
guards.rationale: No AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension anywhere in StrikeDummy.cs, so 3 is the pinned non-ascension value. Re-read against the C# expression rather than against the port's own citation, per PROMPT.md bug class 19 (relics/iron_club.py pinned 6 while its docstring 'quoted' a CardsVar the source sets to 4). C# returns the raw BaseValue and the sim returns the raw int, with no per-hit scaling on either side, so a multi-hit Strike-tagged card (twin_strike) gets +3 PER HIT on both sides -- each hit is its own DamageCmd call.

guards.what: N3: the RETURN CONVENTION -- C# returns 0m to decline, and the sim's dispatcher SUMS listener returns
guards.rationale: Hook.ModifyDamageInternal accumulates `num += num2` over the listeners and records each non-zero contributor in its out-modifiers list (Hook.cs:2515-2524); hooks.py:60-64 sums the same way. strike_dummy.py:32 returns 0 on the decline path, matching StrikeDummy.cs's four `return 0m` bails, so declining adds nothing on either side. The one thing C#'s dispatcher carries that the sim's does not is membership of the modifiers list (which drives Hook.AfterModifyingDamageAmount); Strike Dummy implements no AfterModifyingDamageAmount, so it cannot observe that -- recorded because audit/records/seam/hook_dispatch.json step 38 owns the general case.

guards.what: N4: no state, no reset hook, no IsAllowed override, no presentation members
guards.rationale: StrikeDummy.cs is one override plus one DynamicVar and declares no field, no Flash and no IsAllowed.
